To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a bivariate Markova process is a natural model for the congestion process in computer networks, (ii) an expectation-maximization algorithm can be used to estimate the generator of such a process given a sample path, and (iii) the estimation algorithm is more accurate than an earlier approximate estimation algorithm.

(1) the expectation-maximization algorithm for estimating the parameters of a bivariate finite-state homogeneous continuous-time Markov chain from a sample path of one of its components can be implemented efficiently and accurately; (2) the expectation-maximzation algorithm is more accurate than a time-sampling algorithm; and (3) the time-sampling algorithm is more computationally efficient than the expectation-maximization procedure.

the development of a new model of congestion for networks and the development of an estimation procedure for the parameters of that model.
